claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it ever starts.

In a CodePipeline pipeline with `SUPERSEDED` execution mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, if enough commits land while the stage is busy, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.

Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each run in turn, instead of a later execution superseding an earlier one that never got its turn.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
When defining a CodePipeline pipeline for QUEUED execution mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set, using the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` or `update-pipeline` commands.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource's API docs are located at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ in the Pulumi registry.
The link target https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts-how-it-works.html is an AWS CodePipeline user guide page that describes execution modes.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that prevents concurrent runs of a deployment job targeting that environment.
The link /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ (Pulumi update conflicts troubleshooting page) exists.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, the `lockBehavior` property can be set at the stage level to control how the stage acquires the exclusive lock on the environment it references.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run is run against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack, running one update at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
The link /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ (azuredevops CheckExclusiveLock API docs page) exists.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`, where `command: up` runs pulumi up and `args: --yes` passes the flag.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.

When two concurrent `pulumi up` runs target the same stack, the run that does not obtain the lease fails with an update conflict error (as described in the Pulumi update-conflicts troubleshooting page).
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available, so nothing prevents concurrent builds by default.
The page links to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ as the page describing Pulumi update conflicts.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is 0, meaning unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud provides a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior on a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that a deployment job targets serializes Pulumi deployments so they do not run concurrently.
In Azure Pipelines, the `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage makes runs waiting on an exclusive lock check queue and run in turn.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'Serialize deployments with an exclusive lock' (anchor #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock).
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting that can be set to `QUEUED`, which makes waiting executions run in turn.
In AWS CodePipeline, the default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'Serialize pipeline executions' (anchor #serialize-pipeline-executions).
In TeamCity, the build configuration setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to `1` serializes Pulumi deployment builds so they do not run concurrently.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting labeled 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'Limit concurrent builds' (anchor #limit-concurrent-builds).
